business_problem: BMW needed better data quality, synthetic training data, and lifecycle tooling so plant teams could deploy computer-vision and quality-assurance models quickly across highly variable manufacturing scenarios without depending on scarce AI specialists.
solution_summary: BMW built an end-to-end industrial AI pipeline on NVIDIA DGX systems so its production teams could generate synthetic data, train vision models, and deploy no-code quality applications more quickly. NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise is used to model virtual factories and complex production scenes, which feed the SORDI synthetic-object dataset. DGX systems with Hopper architecture then train both the synthetic-data-generation models and the downstream deep-learning models for detection, segmentation, and classification. BMW manages the broader model lifecycle with NVIDIA Base Command and uses NVIDIA TAO, part of NVIDIA AI Enterprise, for training, inference, and AutoML-driven hyperparameter optimization. The result is a repeatable manufacturing AI workflow that lets employees generate hundreds of thousands of labeled images automatically and push QA automation closer to the shop floor.

TAO and AI Enterprise support training and inference, Base Command orchestrates the lifecycle, and the resulting models are deployed into plant quality workflows such as stitch and door-sill inspection.
